purpose: Single-revision serial phase-share and resource diagnostic for issue 1497; no parallel candidate or speedup claim.
priming: Identical two-second CPU busy loop before each process; outside reported operation timings.
sampling: All repetitions are fresh processes; instrumented spans use Instant and end-of-span /proc/self/status; stream diagnostics so completed work survives a later refusal.
statistic: Retain every process; median successful per-process times and phase shares for three-repeat bounded cells; feasibility cells report outcome and single observation, not a timing distribution.
validity: Only ai-run verdict=CLEAN is usable. Keep contaminated attempts and rerun the complete diagnostic matrix with unchanged protocol; no selective favorable retries. No candidate is being compared.
need_gate: A job family is an implementation priority only if its median share is at least 20% of the completed patched_fourier_transform front-end time in a real-workload-derived cell. Report input-producer time, front-end setup and failed cells separately; no speedup inferred. If region jobs have max width one, classify outer-region scaling unavailable regardless of share.
checks: M6a dense/sample DFT accuracy and full existing result output; IR existing Parseval check/report. These are baseline correctness observations, not a proof of lane determinism. Preserve failures and nonfinite metrics.
limitations: Downscaled cases diagnose the original generators; they do not establish production-resolution efficiency. No tolerance changes, no parallel implementation. Memory estimates and end-of-span RSS are not exact per-phase peak attribution.
validation_runs: Before the matrix, compare the preserved unmodified M6a binary and the diagnostic binary with profiling disabled/enabled on the registered R=4 cell; these are correctness observations, not a speedup experiment.
